{
  "title": "HTTP Cache Semantics: Freshness, Revalidation and Stale Delivery",
  "totalSlides": 3,
  "slides": [
    {
      "slideIndex": 0,
      "title": "HTTP Cache Semantics",
      "section": "HTTP Caching",
      "titleRegister": "label",
      "keyPoints": [
        "Cache-Control directives, ETag-based revalidation, and the bounded conditions for serving stale responses"
      ],
      "suggestedLayout": "Title Slide",
      "contentType": "title",
      "notes": "Use the Standards Ledger direction: restrained standards-document styling, strong rules and callouts, and the proposed preview colours. Keep the cover free of body content."
    },
    {
      "slideIndex": 1,
      "title": "Cache-Control sets the storage and validation contract",
      "section": "HTTP Caching",
      "titleRegister": "label",
      "keyPoints": [
        "Freshness directives determine how long a response can be reused without contacting the origin: max-age for general caches and s-maxage for shared caches.",
        "no-store forbids storing the response; no-cache permits storage but requires successful validation before reuse.",
        "ETag supplies the validator: the client or CDN sends If-None-Match, and the origin returns 304 Not Modified when the representation still matches.",
        "A 304 response reuses the cached representation while updating applicable metadata; it is not a new response body."
      ],
      "suggestedLayout": "Two Column",
      "contentType": "twoColumn",
      "notes": "Use two labelled columns: left, 'Freshness and storage'; right, 'Revalidation with ETag'. Include a compact request/response sequence under the ETag column: cached response becomes stale -> If-None-Match: <etag> -> 304 Not Modified -> cached body reused. Distinguish no-cache from no-store prominently."
    },
    {
      "slideIndex": 2,
      "title": "Stale content is an explicit exception, not a default CDN behavior",
      "section": "HTTP Caching",
      "titleRegister": "label",
      "keyPoints": [
        "A CDN may serve stale content during background validation when stale-while-revalidate authorizes that behavior.",
        "A CDN may serve stale content during an origin failure when stale-if-error applies, subject to its permitted stale window.",
        "A client request with max-stale can permit acceptance of stale content; response directives such as must-revalidate constrain or forbid stale reuse.",
        "Implementation rule: evaluate shared-cache freshness first, then validator-based revalidation, and only then an explicitly permitted stale path."
      ],
      "suggestedLayout": "Title and Content",
      "contentType": "content",
      "notes": "Render the body as a standards-ordered decision path: fresh response -> serve; stale but revalidatable -> send If-None-Match; stale-while-revalidate -> serve stale and validate asynchronously; stale-if-error or max-stale -> serve stale only within the applicable allowance; must-revalidate/no applicable allowance -> do not serve stale. Add a small footer note that s-maxage governs shared-cache freshness when present."
    }
  ],
  "deviations": []
}
